slice: worker subprocess identity and secret isolation
implementation: Exact source-mapped EventBus handlers now receive their named worker DSN and credential without inheriting shared PostgreSQL connection settings or global geospatial provider credentials.
Unmapped legacy handlers retain their existing environment until they receive a dedicated worker identity.
The Kernel supervisor derives its scheduler child allowlist from the canonical scheduled-module worker map, including climate, market-data, sensor-ingestion, and remote-sensing workers.

checks.command: python3 -m pytest tests/test_kernel_runtime_supervisor.py tests/test_worker_environment.py tests/test_event_bus_durability.py tests/test_worker_database.py tests/test_worker_operation_map.py tests/test_scheduler_durability.py tests/test_scheduled_command_contracts.py -q

isolation.database: no database contacted; environment filtering and subprocess invocation are mocked
isolation.providers: no provider calls; only synthetic environment values used

limitations: This closes environment inheritance for the currently mapped EventBus handlers only; unmapped handlers retain legacy settings pending their own identity migrations.
It does not establish live worker credential provisioning, provider delivery, tenant isolation, or RLS and changes no MAN-CAP acceptance status.
